note: Every entry here is a refusal test on a risk path that accepts ANY throw, so a crash in a mis-shaped double satisfies it as well as the refusal does. Registration is not absolution: it records who owns the gap. The ratchet may only go DOWN. Do not add an entry to make a red gate green — name the exception the test actually means. Sites off a risk path are counted as INFO and never registered: banking them would record noise as debt. `.not.toThrow()` and a `.parse()` subject are excluded by a stated rule, not by this file.

allowed.title: fails closed when the tenant GUC is absent
allowed.reason: This assertion lives inside the APP_DATABASE_URL-gated integration describe and does not execute in the normal suite, so the execution triage that produced every other verdict in this gate could not reach it — it is the one site of 220 that recorded no error. Naming a class here would be a guess about what postgres raises when current_org_id() has no GUC, and a guessed class is the defect this gate exists to remove. It becomes tightenable the moment the seeded integration lane runs in CI.

allowed.title: never retrieves settings for a different org when creating a reservation (isolation — deny via tx mock)
allowed.reason: MEASURED, not assumed: this is one of the two sites of 44 that stayed GREEN when every bare .toThrow() in the isolation suite was rewritten to .toThrow(TypeError), i.e. it is satisfied by a crash rather than by the refusal its title claims. The sibling site (invoices payment) was repaired; this one is inventory, which the 10/10 release excludes (accepted residual R-9, review 2026-12-01), so repairing it means editing a module this release does not cover.
